answer: Retrieval‑based dialogue systems now combine context‑response matching with deeper intent modeling, exemplar‑guided paraphrase constraints, and personal‑style conditioning: hierarchical siamese models driven by dialogue‑act sequences and intent‑aware neural ranking improve the relevance of retrieved candidates; structured refinement techniques capture incremental reasoning in multi‑turn chats; exemplar‑based approaches retrieve paraphrase exemplars and enforce generation to stay within their semantic space, yielding more coherent and faithful responses; style‑controlled generation methods inject intimacy or personality embeddings—often learned from personalized dialogue datasets reviewed in 2024—to produce outputs matching a user’s preferred tone; and recent retrieval‑augmented generation frameworks such as GRIP (2026) embed retrieval control tokens directly in the decoder while collaborative‑filtering‑enhanced RAG (2025) leverages user interaction histories for personalized text, together enabling response selection that respects both exemplar paraphrase constraints and individual style.

   A training-based dynamic RAG framework that internalizes retrieval control into token-level decoding.
 ETC [AAAI 2026 Oral Paper]: Modeling Uncertainty Trends for Timely Retrieval in Dynamic RAG  
   A training-free dynamic RAG method that improves retrieval timing by modeling entropy trends during decoding.
 SCD [AAAI 2026 Oral Paper]: Language Drift in Multilingual Retrieval-Augmented Generation  
   A training-free multilingual RAG method that mitigates language drift through decoding-time control. [...] Instead of treating retrieval as an external controller decision, GRIP internalizes retrieval behavior into token-level decoding through explicit control tokens such as `[RETRIEVE]`, `[INTERMEDIARY]`, `[ANSWER]`, and `[SOLVED]`. This design enables the model to decide when to retrieve, how to reformulate follow-up queries, and when to stop, all within a single autoregressive trajectory.

> Related RAG projects from us: GRIP (ACL 2026 Main) · ETC (AAAI 2026 Oral) · SCD (AAAI 2026 Oral)

GRIP is built around a simple idea: retrieval control should be part of generation itself.
